title: Aunty's Bulk Lemon Discount
content: The corner-shop aunty offers 20 extra lemons at half price if you pay today. The school fair is in 3 days. Your savings are down to ₹80 after today's supplies.

choices.text: You pass — keep your ₹80 safe for ice and cups.
choices.scoring_hint: Conservative cash management, prioritises liquidity over margin.

choices.text: You take the full order — bet on the fair rush.
choices.scoring_hint: Aggressive capital deployment, comfort with thin buffer.

choices.text: You ask aunty for 10 lemons at the same discount instead.
choices.scoring_hint: Negotiation instinct, middle path between safety and bet.

title: Diwali Gift Money Decision
content: Your grandparents give you ₹1000 as Diwali gift money. Your business has ₹250 saved. You could double your stock, keep the gift safe, or spend half on a better display board.

choices.text: You stash the full ₹1000 in your savings tin for later.
choices.scoring_hint: Strong capital preservation, low urgency to deploy.

choices.text: You put all ₹1000 into more stock for the holiday week.
choices.scoring_hint: Full reinvestment, growth-first mindset.

choices.text: You spend ₹400 on a painted display board, keep ₹600.
choices.scoring_hint: Balanced — partial reinvestment in assets with buffer intact.

title: Friend Wants to Split Profits
content: Your first week ended with ₹400 profit. Your helper friend Priya says she deserves half because she stood at the stall for two afternoons. You did the buying, cooking, and pricing alone.

choices.text: You give Priya a flat ₹50 thank-you and keep ₹350.
choices.scoring_hint: Values owner effort, cash-thrifty but may strain relationship.

choices.text: You split 50/50 as she asked — ₹200 each.
choices.scoring_hint: Relationship-first, undervalues owner risk.

choices.text: You offer her ₹120 plus a share of next week's profits if she helps again.
choices.scoring_hint: Structured incentive — ties reward to continued effort.

title: Bigger Stall at Ganesh Chaturthi
content: The society is holding a Ganesh Chaturthi mela. A corner stall near the pandal costs ₹200 for the day. A regular stall inside costs ₹50. The corner gets 3x the foot traffic.

choices.text: You book the ₹50 regular stall to stay safe.
choices.scoring_hint: Low-risk expansion, keeps cost floor low.

choices.text: You grab the ₹200 corner stall — bet on the footfall.
choices.scoring_hint: Growth-oriented — invests in position for volume.

choices.text: You team up with your friend Ravi — share the corner stall, split ₹200.
choices.scoring_hint: Shares cost and upside via partnership.

title: Classmate Wants to Join
content: Your friend Rahul sees your crafts selling well and asks to join. He's great at painting but disappears when work gets boring. You currently handle everything yourself.

choices.text: You say no — tell him you'll stick with running it solo.
choices.scoring_hint: Protects control, misses leverage and creative input.

choices.text: You welcome Rahul in as an equal partner on the spot.
choices.scoring_hint: Fast trust extension without guardrails.

choices.text: You give him a 2-week trial on painting only, then decide.
choices.scoring_hint: Structured onboarding — tests before committing.

title: School Canteen Offers a Shelf
content: The school canteen aunty offers you a shelf to sell your friendship bands for a 30% cut of sales. You currently sell 15 bands a week from your bag. The shelf could reach 200 more students.

choices.text: You say no to the cut — keep selling from your bag.
choices.scoring_hint: Keeps margin, ignores distribution upside.

choices.text: You accept the 30% cut and stock the shelf next Monday.
choices.scoring_hint: Trades margin for reach and steady display.

choices.text: You counter-offer 20% for the first month as a trial.
choices.scoring_hint: Negotiates terms and tests the channel before committing.

title: Bookmark Colours Are Bleeding
content: Three customers this week complained that your painted bookmarks smudge when they get damp. You've sold 40 so far at ₹20 each. Switching to waterproof paint costs ₹180 more per batch.

choices.text: You keep the same paint — only 3 people complained.
choices.scoring_hint: Dismisses feedback to protect short-term margin.

choices.text: You switch to waterproof paint and replace all 40 for free.
choices.scoring_hint: Over-corrects — full quality recovery at big cost.

choices.text: You switch paint for new batches and offer replacements only if asked.
choices.scoring_hint: Fixes root cause going forward, measured recovery.

title: Menu Too Long for One Stall
content: Your ice-cream stall sells 6 flavours but only 2 — mango and chocolate — make up 80% of sales. Managing all 6 means a bigger freezer rental (₹150/day) and more leftover stock.

choices.text: You keep all 6 flavours — variety brings curious customers.
choices.scoring_hint: Variety-first, ignores operational cost.

choices.text: You cut to the 2 top sellers only.
choices.scoring_hint: Ruthless focus — maximises unit economics.

choices.text: You run 3 flavours daily — 2 top sellers and a rotating third.
choices.scoring_hint: Balanced — keeps novelty while trimming operational load.

title: Your Best Helper Gets an Offer
content: Your friend Meera, who helps pack crafts every weekend, says another kid offered her ₹100 per weekend to help at his stall — you currently pay her ₹60. She's your most reliable helper.

choices.text: You stick at ₹60 — tell her you hope she stays.
choices.scoring_hint: Hopes for loyalty without matching market.

choices.text: You match the ₹100 right away to keep her.
choices.scoring_hint: Retention-first, responds to market without negotiation.

choices.text: You offer ₹90 plus a share of new-design profits she suggests.
choices.scoring_hint: Retains talent while tying extra pay to value she creates.

title: Cousin Wants to Be Manager
content: Your older cousin Sanjay, who's home for summer holidays, offers to 'manage' your lemonade stand. He wants to make all decisions for the month. He did run the school's sports-day snack counter last year.

choices.text: You hand over full control — he has more experience.
choices.scoring_hint: Over-delegates; gives up founder authority early.

choices.text: You refuse — it's your stall, you'll run it alone.
choices.scoring_hint: Protects control, misses chance to learn from experience.

choices.text: You make him your advisor — he suggests, you decide.
choices.scoring_hint: Retains decision authority while absorbing mentorship.

title: Team Disagreement on New Flavour
content: Your partner Priya insists you launch paan-flavoured ice cream — she thinks it'll go viral at the school fair. You think mango-chilli is safer. Neither of you will budge, and the fair is 4 days away.

choices.text: You overrule her and launch mango-chilli only.
choices.scoring_hint: Decisive but damages partner buy-in.

choices.text: You give in and launch paan to keep the peace.
choices.scoring_hint: Over-accommodates, ignores own conviction.

choices.text: You launch both in small batches and let sales decide.
choices.scoring_hint: Turns disagreement into a test — low-cost experiment.

title: Viral Trend Hits Your Niche
content: A new friendship-band style called 'clay-bead knots' is suddenly everywhere on your cousins' group chat. You've never made them. Stocking the clay beads would cost ₹250 and a full weekend of practice.

choices.text: You ignore the trend — your regular bands are selling fine.
choices.scoring_hint: Stays in lane, misses possible window.

choices.text: You go all-in — ₹250 on beads and a weekend of practice.
choices.scoring_hint: Full trend-chase, commits time and cash to an unproven pivot.

choices.text: You buy ₹80 worth of beads, make 5 samples, test with classmates first.
choices.scoring_hint: Low-cost trend test — validates before scaling.

title: Sibling's Bigger Stall Next Door
content: Your older sibling is setting up a snack stall right next to yours at the society fair, selling samosas and chips. Your lemonade pairs perfectly with their food — but they're also louder and may pull attention away.

choices.text: You move your stall to the other end of the fair, away from them.
choices.scoring_hint: Avoids conflict but also gives up the pairing opportunity.

choices.text: You stay and pitch a 'samosa + lemonade combo' deal together.
choices.scoring_hint: Turns adjacency into a partnership — collaborative upside.

choices.text: You stay but compete hard — lower your price by ₹5 to pull crowd.
choices.scoring_hint: Competitive stance, sacrifices margin against a family stall.

title: Birthday Order Got Mixed Up
content: You delivered 20 chocolate cupcakes to Ananya's birthday — but her mom ordered vanilla. The party starts in 90 minutes. You have 6 vanilla cupcakes left at home and no time to bake more.

choices.text: You apologise and offer a full refund — no replacement.
choices.scoring_hint: Clean exit, but leaves the customer without a solution.

choices.text: You rush the 6 vanilla over, keep the chocolate there as a bonus, and refund 30%.
choices.scoring_hint: Salvages the event with creative recovery and partial refund.

choices.text: You argue that chocolate is better and refuse to budge.
choices.scoring_hint: Denies the mistake, damages trust and future orders.

title: Holi Rainout Cancels the Fair
content: Heavy unseasonal rain on Holi weekend cancels the society mela. You've already paid ₹150 for the stall spot and made 80 packets of coloured rangoli powder — they don't spoil but won't sell till next year.

choices.text: You pack everything up and wait a whole year to sell next Holi.
choices.scoring_hint: Accepts loss passively, no alternate distribution.

choices.text: You post in the society WhatsApp group with a 20% discount for door delivery.
choices.scoring_hint: Pivots channel quickly to recover some of the cost.

choices.text: You donate the rangoli to the school art club and claim it as learning.
choices.scoring_hint: Writes off stock for goodwill — low cash recovery, reputation gain.
